Vibe coding, for project management.

Tell PM Codex what happened, in plain words: a meeting, a slipped date, a new risk. Its AI assistant updates the tasks, risks, timeline and minutes for you, and every change waits for your sign-off. It runs on your own computer and keeps your data in your own Google Sheet.

Modules

10 screens, one Google Sheet

Everything a project manager keeps, grouped the way the app's module bar groups it. The Overview pulls the late, the blocked and the due-this-week from all of them. These are the app's own screens; each one opens in the demo above.

Timeline

Plan

A Gantt chart and an Excel-style activity sheet with formulas, WORKDAY and NETWORKDAYS included. Save a revision and compare the plan against it.

Deliverables

Plan

What the project hands over, with owners, due dates and a definition of done. A deliverable can hold its own sub-deliverables.

Tasks & Issues

Track

Action items and issues by status or owner, with priority, flags, comments and links to the timeline. Late dates turn magenta.

Risks

Track

A register with a heat map drawn from your own risk matrix. Grade each risk before and after mitigation, and click a cell to list what's in it.

MoM

Meet

Minutes with agenda, decisions and action items you push to the tracker when you're ready. Gemini can draft them from a recording, in any language.

Stakeholders

People

Who matters and how much: power, interest and knowledge, with a power and interest grid, an org chart and a Venn of groups.

Documents

Records

One register for the project's documents: type, version, status, owner and a link to the file.

Codex

Records

The knowledge base: folders of pages with the rules and decisions every assistant reads before it suggests anything.

Billing

Records

Payment milestones with work, document and invoice status, and a quarterly projection of what's billed and what's still to come. Off until you turn it on in Settings.

Change requests

2 assistants, 1 review

PM Codex works with two assistants: Claude, from the Claude desktop app, and Gemini, built into the app. Neither one writes to your project. Whatever an assistant wants to change arrives as a change request, and every line in it shows what the value was and what it becomes.

  1. 01

    The assistant reads

    Either assistant sees the project the way you do: modules, records and the Codex.

  2. 02

    It files one request

    Every change it wants goes into a single change request, waiting for you in the app.

  3. 03

    You review

    Each line opens on the record it changes, old value above new. Edit it, or untick it to decline.

  4. 04

    You sign off

    The ticked lines apply and save to your Sheet. The assistant is told what you approved and what you didn't.

Both assistants' requests use the same review panel and the same four marks, in every module. A line you edit before signing off stays yours: no assistant can overwrite it with a new proposal.

They also share one standing brief: read first, ask before assuming, keep it short. Each picks a cartridge for the problem in front of it and logs it.

Privacy glossary

Names never reach the AI as names

List the names you would rather keep to yourself: people, clients, vendors, systems. Before anything is sent to Claude or Gemini, every listed name, and every variation of it, becomes a token such as [Redacted_Name_1]. The answer comes back in tokens, and the app turns them back into the real names on your screen.

  • Both assistants. Claude through the bridge, Gemini in the sidebar: the same glossary masks everything each one reads, and turns back what each one proposes.
  • One per project. Each project keeps its own list, so a client in one project is not a token in another. When Claude reads another project, that project's glossary masks it.
  • The AI never guesses. It works with the tokens and refers to people by their role, never asking who a token stands for.

  1. 01On your screen

    Ask Hana Okafor to approve the budget for Kestrel Foods.

  2. 02What the AI receives

    Ask [Redacted_Name_1] to approve the budget for [Redacted_Organization_1].

  3. 03What it proposes

    New task: "Chase [Redacted_Name_1] for the budget sign-off"

  4. 04What you review and keep

    Chase Hana Okafor for the budget sign-off

Add a name — three ways

  1. Select it, anywhere

    Select a name in any record, page or set of minutes. A shield button appears above it. Choose Create new and its type, or Add as variation of a name already listed, then Save.

  2. From Settings

    Open Settings → Privacy glossary and click New entry. Type the term and pick its type: Name, Organization, Email, Phone, Location, Application or Other. The token is made for you from the type.

  3. Caught as you type

    In any text box, a listed name is marked as protected while you type. A near miss, a typo or another spelling, is marked too: “Did you mean Hana Okafor? It will be masked as [Redacted_Name_1].”

Keep it in shape

Variations
Open an entry and click the pencil to add nicknames, initials, full names and common misspellings: Hana, H. Okafor, HO. Each one gets the entry's token. Matching ignores capital letters.
Find and edit
Search the list or filter it by type. Change an entry's term, type, variations or notes from its panel, or delete it with the bin. Changing the type gives it a fresh token.
One token, one name
Two entries in a project never share a token: the app will not finish an edit that would make a duplicate, so every token turns back into the right name.
Before you paste
The glossary masks the words you list, exactly as listed. A name that is not on the list is sent as written. Before you paste a meeting transcript or an email thread, add the people and companies in it.

Your data

Your machine, your Sheet
The app
Runs on your own computer at http://localhost:7800, installed and started by Pinokio. Nothing is hosted for you.
Your data
Lives in a Google Sheet you own, through an Apps Script you deploy yourself. The Sheet keeps its own version history.
The Gemini key
Stays in the small local server that forwards Gemini calls. It never reaches the page, and the server refuses to start if a build ever carries it.
The archive
Finished tasks, deliverables and risks you archive drop out of what the AI sees by default. It can still read them when it asks.

Privacy glossary

Names you list are swapped for tokens before anything reaches the AI, and swapped back on your screen. Each project keeps its own list.

How to add and manage names

Install

Mac now, Windows later

What you need

  • A Mac
  • Pinokio, the free app that installs and runs local apps
  • A Google account, for your own Sheet
  • A Gemini API key (optional)
  • The Claude desktop app (optional)

Install and start

  1. 01

    Open PM Codex on Pinokio, or in Pinokio open Discover and search for PM Codex. You can also download from this address:

    https://github.com/Ashvall01/PM-Codex
  2. 02

    Click Install.

  3. 03

    Click Start. A Gemini key is optional — add it later in the app.

  4. 04

    Click Open PM Codex. The first time, the setup wizard walks you through making your Sheet and connecting it.

Connect to Claude

  1. 01Install the Claude desktop app.
  2. 02In Pinokio, PM Codex, click Connect to Claude, then Install in the window Claude shows.
  3. 03Keep PM Codex open. In a new Claude conversation, say “Start a PM Codex session.”

Three rules

  1. 1One browser tab only. Each tab saves your whole Sheet, so two tabs overwrite each other.
  2. 2Always use http://localhost:7800. A different address starts an empty app.
  3. 3Keep the Sheet's web app address private. Anyone who has it can read your data.
